testCase.description: DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: "number("1.1") = number("1.1", null, null) = 1.1". Normative example of the new single-parameter number(from) for a string.
DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: "number("1.1") = number("1.1", null, null) = 1.1". Normative equivalence of the single-parameter form with null separators.
DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "number": "return from" (DMN16-105); example "number(5) = 5".
DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "number": "return from" (DMN16-105). Derived: number(-1.5) = -1.5 (a negative decimal is returned unchanged).

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); §10.3.2.13.5 "If named, unsupplied parameters are bound to null". number(from: "1.1") = 1.1 under either the one- or three-parameter signature.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any"; rule 35 numeric literal = [ "-" ] , ( digits , [ ".", digits ] | "." , digits ) .... Derived: number("-12") = -12.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); rule 35 numeric literal allows "." , digits. Edge: number(".5") = 0.5.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any". With a null grouping separator nothing is removed and "1,000.0" is not a numeric literal, so number("1,000.0") = null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any". With a null grouping separator the space is not removed, so number("1 000") = null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any". "abc" is not a numeric literal; DMN 1.6 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." number("abc") = null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any". Edge: the empty string is not a numeric literal, so number("") = null.
DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) domains are "string" and "number"; DMN 1.6 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." number(null) = null.
DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) domains are "string" and "number"; DMN 1.6 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." number(true) = null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) domains are "string" and "number"; DMN 1.6 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." number(date("2024-01-01")) = null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters") gives 42 and number(from) with domain "number": "return from" (DMN16-105) returns it. Edge: number(number("42")) = 42.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters") and number(from) with domain "number": "return from" (DMN16-105); DMN16-105: "helps in situations where expressions produce, e.g. a string or a number". Edge: for x in ["5", 5] return number(x) = [5, 5].
DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "number": "return from" (DMN16-105). Edge: the result of an arithmetic expression is returned unchanged, number(10 / 4) = 2.5.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208: "reuse the existing semantics of passing in null for the second and third parameters"); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any". Rule 35 numeric literal = [ "-" ] , ... has no leading "+" (nor does rule 37 digits), so from is outside its domain; DMN 1.6 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." Edge: number("+5") = null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.1 Table 73: number(from) with domain "string" (DMN16-208); footnote 1: "from SHALL conform to grammar rule 37 [numeric literal, rule 35 in this edition], after removing all occurrences of the grouping separator, if any". Rule 35 numeric literal requires digits after the decimal point (digits , [ ".", digits ]), so from is outside its domain; DMN 1.6 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." Edge: number("1.") = null.
